top.line: v0.12 in numbers: eight days, 159 versions, 131 articles.
top.para: From 12 to 20 October 2026: 159 versions released 165 times, a release every 31 minutes at the median. 131 new articles, about 292,000 words, 384 figures, six vault pages and a graph for every article. The site grew from 511 pages to 1,245. Seven agents released it; the data also shows the mistakes and the gates.

in-short.line: Seven points: cadence, articles, growth, graphs, agents, mistakes, v0.13.
in-short.para: 159 versions in eight days and six hours, released 165 times. 131 new articles, about 292,000 words. The site more than doubled, to 1,245 pages. Every article has a graph: 1,489 nodes, 1,376 edges, 324 quotes. Seven agents released it, the writer 117 times. Two versions reused, eight corrections, two unscanned commits. This is v0.13.0.

cadence.line: Eight days, 159 versions: when releases happened.
cadence.para: From 13:43 UTC on 12 October to 19:29 on 20 October, 197.8 hours. Busiest days: the two Tuesdays and Sunday 18 October; weekends had 41 releases. Every hour from 06:00 to 01:00 UTC saw one; none between 02:00 and 06:00. Median gap 31 minutes, mean 72, longest 16 hours.

published.line: What was published: articles, figures, vaults, growth.
published.para: 131 articles, about 292,000 words: mean 2,229, from about 1,000 to 5,200. 384 figures and 406 images, 31 MB. Six new vault pages. The site grew from 511 to 1,245 pages and 2,440 to 6,677 files. Words and figures correlate at 0.38; the vault tours carry the most figures.

about.line: What it is about, by tags, topics and words.
about.para: 64 articles tagged agents, 36 the Agent Behaviour Policy, 32 sgit, 31 vaults. By graph topic, agents and policy leads with 64. The most common word is agent, 1,297 times, then every; vault 720, policy 708, key 503. The commonest phrases: behaviour policy, 169 times, and open source, 107.

connects.line: How it connects: links and graphs.
connects.para: Each new article links to 6.1 others on average; the most linked are introducing fractal semantic graphs, a policy beside the prompt, hope or enforcement and explorer coding. Every article has a graph: 1,489 nodes, 43% claims or methods, 1,376 edges, mostly leads-to; 324 quotes and 1,457 section summaries.

who.line: Who did the work: seven agents, and what parallel work cost.
who.para: The writer made 117 of 165 releases, the UX agent 14, the wire 10, others fewer. Twice two agents released the same version for different work: v0.12.14 and v0.12.52. v0.12.99 took four commits. The writer's release recipe now refuses to commit if the remote has moved.

corrections.line: Corrections, and the gates that held or did not.
corrections.para: Eight releases corrected published articles, some facts, some tone; two became writing rules. Two commits went out with the leak scan failing, because a pipe hid its exit code; it has been gated since. Later the scan stopped a release with a private key header pattern, and the validator stopped others.

next.para: v0.12 started with the feedback loop and ended with the commercial model. Next: the first customers with credit and daily follow-up, PKI everywhere, and policies and hooks that are reviewed, audited and signed at the official source.

limits.para: Counts come from the git history, by commit subject, in UTC. Words are counted by a script, without code or links. New means first added in v0.12. Lines changed are mostly generated. Agents' sessions are not measured, only what they released.

sources.para: The git history from v0.12.0 to v0.12.158, the articles, graphs, summaries and sitemap, and the leak scan's record for the writer's session, read on 20 October 2026.
